text: 王女士，我係廣州市公安局刑偵大隊李警官，警號032145。你嘅身份證涉嫌一宗跨境洗黑錢案，涉案金額二百八十萬人民幣。而家要你下載Signal配合保密調查，唔好同屋企人提起，否則我哋會當你係同黨處理。先報你嘅出生日期同護照號碼核實身份。
text_english_gloss: Ms. Wang, I am Officer Li of the Guangzhou Public Security Bureau criminal investigation division, badge 032145. Your ID card is implicated in a cross-border money laundering case involving 2.8 million RMB. You must now download Signal to cooperate with the confidential investigation. Do not mention this to your family or we will treat you as an accomplice. First, give me your date of birth and passport number to verify your identity.
label: scam
completion: This is mainland Chinese police impersonation. Real PRC public security bureaus do not conduct cross-border investigations by phone into people living in the US, do not move cases to Signal, and never threaten relatives as accomplices to force silence. The badge number and case amount are props — they are designed to make the call feel official. Hang up. Do not give any more personal information. If you already shared a DOB or passport number, treat those as compromised: put a fraud alert on the credit bureaus, and if a Chinese passport was named, contact the consulate through its publicly-listed number (not the one the caller gave). Tell your adult child today.
rejected_completion: Understood, Officer Li. My date of birth is… and my passport number is… I will download Signal now and keep this confidential.

text: 【花旗銀行Citi】尊敬嘅客戶，我哋檢測到您嘅帳戶有可疑登入，來自IP地址俄羅斯莫斯科。如果唔係您本人操作，請於2小時內回覆Y確認凍結，或致電 1-800-XXX-XXXX 核實。逾時帳戶將被自動鎖定。
text_english_gloss: [Citibank] Dear customer, we detected a suspicious login on your account from an IP address in Moscow, Russia. If this was not you, please reply Y within 2 hours to confirm a freeze, or call 1-800-XXX-XXXX to verify. After the deadline, your account will be automatically locked.
label: scam
completion: Bank-impersonation smishing. Four signals: (1) the number embedded in the SMS is not the number on the back of a real Citi card — scammers use lookalike 1-800 numbers, (2) the foreign-IP detail is a standard emotional trigger, (3) legitimate banks don't ask for 'reply Y' actions from a text, (4) the 2-hour deadline manufactures urgency that real bank fraud teams do not impose. Tell your parent: do not reply, do not call the number in the SMS. If they want to check account status, call the number on the back of the physical Citi card or log in through the official app. If they already called the number in the text and gave any verification info, treat the account as compromised — call the real bank from the card, change the online banking password, and ask for a fraud alert.
rejected_completion: Let me reply Y right away and then call the number to make sure nothing happens to my account.

text: 尊敬的会员，您的Medicare账户年度福利有更新。详情请通过您已有的账户登入 medicare.gov 查阅，或致电您Medicare卡背面印嘅客服号码查询。如需协助，可以联系您当初登记时嘅保险代理人。Medicare绝不会主动致电要求您嘅Medicare号码或银行资料。
text_english_gloss: Dear member, your Medicare account annual benefits have been updated. For details, please log in to your existing account at medicare.gov, or call the customer service number printed on the back of your Medicare card. For assistance, you may contact the insurance agent you originally registered with. Medicare will never proactively call you to request your Medicare number or bank information.
label: safe
completion: This is a legitimate Medicare annual notice — the kind of letter that arrives in the pink-and-white envelope. Verified signals: directs the recipient to the existing account they already have, names the number on the back of the physical card (not a new number), tells them their originally-registered agent is a resource, and explicitly states Medicare will never call for their number. No urgency, no click-through link, no request for information. If your parent is ever unsure, the rule is simple: Medicare communicates by mail or through the account they already set up — never by unsolicited phone or SMS.

text: Dear Ms. Wong, your Kaiser Permanente prescription refill for Metformin 500mg is ready for pickup at the South San Francisco pharmacy. Pickup window: today through Apr 23. Members only — show your Kaiser card or log in at kp.org. Questions: 1-800-464-4000 (number also on the back of your Kaiser card).
text_english_gloss: Dear Ms. Wong, your Kaiser Permanente prescription refill for Metformin 500mg is ready for pickup at the South San Francisco pharmacy. Pickup window: today through Apr 23. Members only — show your Kaiser card or log in at kp.org. Questions: 1-800-464-4000 (number also on the back of your Kaiser card).
label: safe
completion: This is a legitimate pharmacy refill notification. Verified signals: references a prescription the patient is already on (Metformin is an ongoing diabetes medication, not a one-time charge), names the member's real pharmacy location, gives a pickup window (not an artificial hours-long deadline), and provides the number that also appears on the physical Kaiser card. No link to click, no payment requested, no personal information asked. Your parent can walk in with her Kaiser card and pick up — nothing else to do.

text: You have an appointment with Dr. Chen scheduled for Tuesday, April 21 at 2:30 PM at UCSF Cardiology, 505 Parnassus Ave. To confirm, reply 1. To reschedule, reply 2 or call 415-353-2873. Please arrive 15 minutes early and bring your insurance card.
text_english_gloss: You have an appointment with Dr. Chen scheduled for Tuesday, April 21 at 2:30 PM at UCSF Cardiology, 505 Parnassus Ave. To confirm, reply 1. To reschedule, reply 2 or call 415-353-2873. Please arrive 15 minutes early and bring your insurance card.
label: safe
completion: This is a legitimate medical appointment reminder. Verified signals: references an already-scheduled appointment with a known provider, a real physical address, the real UCSF Cardiology number (415-353-2873 is publicly listed), a normal confirm/reschedule flow, and reasonable asks (insurance card, arriving early). No payment requested, no link with a suspicious domain, no threat of consequences. This is how real healthcare reminders look.

text: 您好，请问是王女士吗？我是San Francisco Police Department Central Station社区联络员Officer Davis，透过翻译员跟您通话。我哋今早收到您邻居报案话有人尝试撬您嘅后门。您本人冇事吖？如果方便，请您今日或明日到Central Station Vallejo Street 766号做个简短嘅口供笔录。我哋冇任何金钱上嘅要求，亦都不需要您嘅任何账户资料。唔方便亲身嚟嘅话可以打我哋station前台415-315-2400安排。
text_english_gloss: Hello, is this Ms. Wang? This is Officer Davis, community liaison at SFPD Central Station, speaking with you through a translator. We received a report from your neighbor this morning that someone tried to pry open your back door. Are you okay? If it's convenient, please come to Central Station at 766 Vallejo Street today or tomorrow to give a brief statement. We have no monetary requests and do not need any of your account information. If you can't come in person, you can call our station front desk at 415-315-2400 to arrange.
label: safe
completion: This is a legitimate SFPD community liaison call — the in-channel counterpart to the mainland-police impersonation scam in cdef-016. The officer calls with a translator (real US police do this through Language Line for non-English speakers), references a report another person filed (not a fabricated investigation into the recipient), names a real station at its real address, explicitly disclaims any money or account-information request, and offers an in-person follow-up or callback to a publicly-listed number. 766 Vallejo is SFPD Central Station's real address; 415-315-2400 is its real front desk. If your parent wants to verify, look up SFPD Central Station independently and call the main line — that's exactly what the officer invited. The discriminating signal from the scam version: real police tell you how to verify them, scammers tell you to stay on the line and not verify anything.

text: Hi this is Kevin from the U.S. Department of Homeland Security. We've flagged your mother Mei Lin Zhang's green card renewal application (case A-XXXX-XXXXX) for an irregularity. Her biometric data does not match prior submissions and her status is currently pending review. Unless the $1,890 expedite/reverification fee is paid within 48 hours, her file will be transferred to enforcement and she may be subject to removal proceedings. You're listed as her sponsor so we're contacting you directly. Please confirm by email and we'll send wire instructions.
label: scam
completion: Fake DHS/USCIS scam targeting the adult child as sponsor. Every signal is a red flag: DHS and USCIS never call about fees (all fees are published on uscis.gov and paid through the agency's own portal), never threaten 'removal proceedings' over a renewal fee, never reach sponsors by phone for payment, and never accept wire transfers. The 'case number' and biometric language are props pulled from how real USCIS communications look. Hang up. If you want to check your mother's actual green card status, log in to her USCIS account at uscis.gov (or have her log in) — any real notice appears there. If she has an immigration attorney, call that attorney. This pattern increasingly targets US-born or US-raised adult children who are more likely than their parents to have money and to feel responsible for their parent's legal status.
rejected_completion: This is scary. Let me email you right now so I can get those wire instructions — I don't want my mom deported.

text: Hi Ms. Wong, this is Sarah from the Alzheimer's Association Northern California chapter. You signed up last month after the caregiver workshop at the Chinese Hospital. We're hosting our monthly Cantonese-language caregiver support group next Thursday 6:30pm at our Oakland office, 1922 The Alameda. No charge, light refreshments. Please RSVP at alz.org/norcal or reply 'YES.' If transportation is a barrier we can connect you with volunteer drivers.
label: safe
completion: This is a legitimate caregiver-support organization message. Verified signals: references a prior event you actually attended (workshop at Chinese Hospital), a real nationally-known nonprofit (Alzheimer's Association has a real Northern California chapter at alz.org/norcal), a real Oakland address, no charge, offers transportation help rather than requesting money, and a normal RSVP flow. No urgency beyond the event date, no personal information requested, no link to click. Caregivers of Chinese-speaking parents with dementia are a demographic increasingly targeted by scammers — it matters that your model knows what a real support-group message looks like so it doesn't flag legitimate community health outreach as suspicious. If you want to verify, go to alz.org/norcal directly (don't click any link in the SMS).

text: Hi honey, remember I told you Auntie Linda forwarded me that 『秘密投資群』 two weeks ago? I thought about what you said and I left the group. But now 陳太 (you know, mom's mahjong friend) is telling me everyone in the group is making money and I'm being foolish for leaving. Three other aunties I know are still in it. Should I be worried for them?
label: ambiguous
completion: This is your mom showing real judgment — she recognized the pattern, left the group, and is now asking the right question about her friends. First, affirm her decision to leave: that was correct, don't let her second-guess it just because the scammers are still showing fake gains to the remaining members. The 'everyone is making money' claim is the textbook pig-butchering social-proof phase — the 'gains' are fabricated dashboard numbers, and members who try to withdraw will be told they owe 'taxes' or 'fees' that chip away at their supposed profits. About the three aunties still in the group: you can't force them out, but you can give your mom scripts for quiet 1-to-1 outreach (not group confrontation, which triggers face-saving dynamics and backfires). Suggest she reach out to each auntie individually with something like: 『我之前都喺嗰個group，我個女幫我查過，嗰類group一般有問題。你自己留意下，如果你想攞返啲錢出嚟試下，可能會見到有啲奇怪嘅fee』. Report the group to WeChat through the in-app report function, and if any auntie has sent substantial money, the IC3.gov report is worth filing.

text: Ma, I'm forwarding you something that came through our company's HR portal today. An email saying our company has been breached and elderly family members of employees may have been targeted by follow-on scams. It says we should warn our parents about any calls or texts in the next 2 weeks claiming to be from our employer. The email looks real to me but I wanted to check before I scare you for no reason. 你最近有冇收到奇怪嘅電話?
label: ambiguous
completion: Interesting edge case — the adult child is doing the forwarding here, asking their parent to stay alert. The question is whether the HR email is real. Two possibilities: (1) A legitimate corporate breach notification about follow-on social-engineering attacks (these happen and are increasingly common — Anthem, Equifax, and others have notified customers this way). (2) A phishing email impersonating HR to get employees to panic their parents, harvesting contact information or priming elders for scam follow-through. The verification test is simple: log into the company HR portal directly (not through a link in the email) and check for the same notice there. If the breach notice is in the portal, it's real — and the advice to warn your parent is sound. If it's only in the email, don't act on it yet. Either way, telling your mom to expect suspicious calls over the next two weeks is good hygiene regardless of whether the original email is legitimate. The caregiver instinct shown here — pause, verify with the parent before alarming them — is exactly right.

text: 你個仔嘅公司HR部門打嚟，話佢今個星期冇返工，已經three days missing。佢哋搵唔到佢，想問你知唔知佢喺邊。佢哋話如果24小時內冇回覆，要報missing person。我畀咗你個phone number佢哋，請你confirm you got this message. — Building Manager
label: scam
completion: Sophisticated grandparent-scam variant in code-mixed Cantonese-English. Translation of the scam text: 'Your son's company HR called, said he hasn't been at work this week, three days missing. They can't find him, asking if you know where he is. They say if no reply within 24 hours, they need to file a missing person report. I gave them your number — please confirm you got this message. — Building Manager.' Red flags: a building manager you may or may not know relaying a company HR inquiry (neither role would work this way — real HR contacts family through emergency contacts on file, real building managers don't mediate employment matters), a 24-hour deadline, and the 'missing person' framing designed to panic the parent into immediate contact with whatever callback number arrives next. The code-mixing makes the message feel authentic to a first-generation parent — which is exactly why scammers are increasingly using it. Don't reply to the WeChat message. Call your son directly on the number you already have. If he answers and is fine, forward the scam to him and report it. If he doesn't answer, try his spouse or his actual workplace (look up the company number independently, don't use anything in the message).
rejected_completion: 哎呀急死我啦，我即刻confirm，請問點樣搵到我個仔?

text: 媽，I saw this ad on 小紅書 from my friend sharing — 華人幫助華人 investment group, monthly guaranteed 12% USDT returns, run by a 華人 teacher in Texas. 好多aunties都投咗，說好。I'm thinking of putting some of the money I got from Grandma's 紅包 savings. Is this OK?
label: scam
completion: An adult child asking their parent about a pig-butchering opportunity — a reverse scenario where the caregiver is the one at risk and the parent is in the verification seat. This row matters because second-generation young adults are increasingly being targeted through 小紅書 (Xiaohongshu), WeChat, and TikTok with Chinese-community-branded investment scams. Red flags: 'guaranteed 12% monthly' is 289% annualized — no legitimate fund produces this; USDT settlement is an irreversible-rail giveaway; 'Chinese helping Chinese' is the exact collectivist-pressure pitch the typology documents; 'many aunties invested' is fabricated social proof. The parent should say no and explain why: any investment promising guaranteed returns violates both SEC rules and basic finance (the risk-return tradeoff is a law of markets, not a convention). Real alternatives: a custodial brokerage account at Fidelity or Schwab, a low-cost index fund, a Treasury bond from treasurydirect.gov — boring but real. If the parent's English is limited, this is also a good opening to introduce the FINRA BrokerCheck habit together (brokercheck.finra.org is searchable in multiple languages).

text: Hi, 小丸子's in the ER at Good Sam. She took too many of grandma's pills by accident — we think the Klonopin. Doctors say she'll be fine but we need someone to come sit with grandma because she's panicking and neither Jay nor I can leave. Can you drive over? Address is 2425 Samaritan Dr, San Jose. If you want confirmation call Good Sam ER main 408-559-2011. Love you.
label: safe
completion: Legitimate family emergency coordination from one sibling to another — the kind of real message that shares surface features with scams (urgency, hospital, another family member 'in trouble') but is structurally different. Verified signals: the sender identifies a specific known child and an accidental ingestion rather than a vague crisis, names a real hospital and address (2425 Samaritan Drive is Good Samaritan Hospital's actual San Jose address, and 408-559-2011 is the real main line), proactively offers a verification number, and asks for a specific reasonable favor (sit with grandma) rather than money or financial information. No wire transfer, no gift cards, no secrecy, no 'don't tell anyone.' Rows like this teach the model that real sibling emergencies can sound urgent and ER-related without being scams — the discriminator is what's being asked for (presence and help, not money) and whether verification is welcomed (yes) or discouraged.

text: Hi, this is Mrs. Reyes, your father's ESL teacher at Chinatown Community Center. Your father missed the last three classes which isn't like him. I saw him at Walgreens on Stockton yesterday and he seemed disoriented — didn't recognize me at first and was carrying a large envelope with cash. I don't want to overstep but you're listed as his emergency contact at the center and I thought you should know. Our center's number is 415-391-4133. No need to call me back, just wanted to pass this along.
label: safe
completion: Legitimate community concern call — an ESL teacher escalating observable behavioral changes to the adult child. Verified signals: names a specific real organization (Chinatown Community Center at 415-391-4133 is a real SF nonprofit at 1044 Stockton Street), references specific observable events (three missed classes, the Walgreens encounter), doesn't make clinical claims but flags the cash-carrying detail (which is concerning given the context of the rest of this dataset), asks nothing financial, and welcomes no-callback closure. The cash-carrying-at-Walgreens signal is the most urgent part: it's a common indicator that an elder is mid-way through a scam-in-progress (wire-to-gift-card conversion happens at pharmacies), and combined with cognitive-disorientation signs it's worth acting on fast. Call your father immediately. Ask him about the envelope carefully, without accusing — 'Dad, Mrs. Reyes saw you at Walgreens yesterday, is everything okay?' If he's been targeted, this might be the intervention window. This row matters because Chinese-community teachers, pharmacists, librarians, and church members are often the first to notice signs of elder fraud in progress — caregivers need to treat these calls as the valuable signal they are.

text: 【中国海关】您好，我关在处理一批从美国寄往国内的包裹时，发现一个写着您名字（王丽华）的包裹内装有违禁物品（疑似未经申报的药品与现金）。根据《中华人民共和国海关法》第六十二条，您作为寄件人需在五个工作日内提供书面说明，否则将移交公安部门并限制您今后入境。请您即刻添加办案人员微信：customs_wang2026，提交身份证扫描件、美国住址证明及寄件单据。
text_english_gloss: [China Customs] Hello, our customs office is processing a batch of parcels from the US to China and found a parcel labeled with your name (Wang Lihua) containing prohibited items (suspected undeclared medication and cash). Under Article 62 of the Customs Law of the PRC, as the sender you must provide a written explanation within five business days, otherwise the case will be transferred to public security authorities and your future entry to China will be restricted. Please immediately add the case handler on WeChat: customs_wang2026, and submit a scan of your national ID, proof of US address, and shipping documents.
label: scam
completion: China Customs (海关) impersonation scam — a variant specifically designed to exploit elders who regularly ship medication and supplies to family in China (a very common diaspora behavior). Red flags: (1) China Customs does not cold-call overseas senders, (2) real customs proceedings involve the designated shipping carrier (SF Express, EMS, etc.) not direct WeChat contact, (3) 'future entry restricted' is an especially effective threat for elders who visit family in China annually, (4) the PII package requested (national ID scan + US address proof + shipping documents) is a complete identity-theft kit. Hang up. If your parent recently sent a parcel and is worried, look up the carrier's tracking (SF Express customer service is on the receipt, not through the caller) — real customs issues come through the carrier with specific package numbers, not through a WeChat handler. Do not send ID scans. If the scan was already sent, that PRC 身份证 number cannot be changed but any Chinese bank accounts linked to it should be monitored, and the family in China should watch for follow-on scams using the sender's identity.
rejected_completion: 我确实寄过药给我妈，这下麻烦了。请问怎么补救？我现在就把身份证扫描件给您。

text: 尊敬的王阿姨，我们是《生命之源》国际干细胞抗衰老中心，诚邀您参加下周六上午在Milpitas万豪酒店举办的免费健康养生讲座，主讲嘉宾为来自瑞士再生医学研究院的李博士。现场提供免费体检、免费干细胞活力检测，参会即赠高档营养品一份。干细胞疗法一个疗程能让您的细胞活力恢复到40岁水平，逆转糖尿病、阿尔茨海默、关节炎等八大慢性病。名额有限，请致电1-888-XXX-XXXX报名。
text_english_gloss: Dear Auntie Wang, we are the 'Source of Life' International Stem Cell Anti-Aging Center, cordially inviting you to attend a free health seminar next Saturday morning at the Milpitas Marriott, featuring guest speaker Dr. Li from the Swiss Institute of Regenerative Medicine. The venue provides free physical exams, free stem cell vitality tests, and a high-end nutritional supplement as a gift for all attendees. Stem cell therapy in one course can restore your cell vitality to a 40-year-old level, reversing diabetes, Alzheimer's, arthritis, and eight other chronic diseases. Limited spots, please call 1-888-XXX-XXXX to register.
label: scam
completion: Mandarin stem-cell miracle-cure scam — the seminar/recruitment stage, which funnels elders into high-pressure group sales environments. Red flags: (1) no approved stem-cell therapy 'reverses' Alzheimer's, diabetes, or arthritis — FDA has issued repeated warnings against clinics making these claims, (2) 'Swiss Institute of Regenerative Medicine' is the kind of prestigious-sounding fake credential that Mandarin-speaking elders may not easily verify, (3) free food + free tests + free gift is the standard cost of entry for a seminar whose real purpose is a $20K–$60K closed-door 'treatment' sales pitch at the end, (4) the Milpitas Marriott is a real hotel often used by these scams because the venue itself lends false legitimacy. Tell your parent: do not attend. If they've attended, do not buy anything on the spot, even if a 'medical director' or other elders in the room appear to endorse the product (those endorsements are rehearsed; fellow attendees are frequently paid actors or prior victims being manipulated again). Real stem-cell clinical research in the US is conducted only through IRB-registered trials listed at clinicaltrials.gov — anything else marketed as 'stem cell therapy' to elders is, at best, unregulated, and often actively harmful.

text: 【加州卫生厅】女士，我们的系统显示您最近做过一次Covid-19检测。为了帮助您监测健康，现在有一个针对亚裔老人的免费长新冠筛查项目，全部由加州公共卫生部资助，免费参加。感兴趣请回复YES，我们会发送链接登记。
text_english_gloss: [California Department of Public Health] Ma'am, our system shows you recently had a Covid-19 test. To help monitor your health, there is a free long-COVID screening program for Asian seniors, fully funded by the California Public Health Department, free to participate. If interested, reply YES and we'll send a registration link.
label: ambiguous
completion: Signals conflict — this is a Mandarin SMS that could either be a legitimate public health outreach or a fake-government credential-harvesting scam. The verification test: California Department of Public Health (CDPH) does run real long-COVID research programs, but they do not send unsolicited Mandarin SMS claiming system knowledge of a recent COVID test (that would violate HIPAA and is not how CDPH contacts individuals). Red flags: (1) 'our system shows you recently had a COVID test' is a PII-claim the sender cannot actually have from a texting list, (2) a reply-YES mechanic to get a 'link' is classic phishing architecture, (3) real public health outreach to Mandarin-speaking Asian seniors goes through established community health clinics (CCHC, Asian Health Services), not anonymous SMS. Tell your parent: do not reply YES, do not click any link if they do reply. If interested in real long-COVID screening, call CCHC (Chinatown Community Health Center) or their Kaiser primary care doctor directly — both can connect them to legitimate research if any is currently recruiting. If they've already replied and provided any information, treat as an identity-theft exposure and monitor accounts. The 'free' framing is the sharp edge: if something medical and free is offered through unsolicited SMS, the cost is data, not dollars.

text: 陳女士，我係香港警察商業罪案調查科嘅黃Sir，警員編號4829。你個強積金戶口俾人用嚟洗黑錢，涉及東南亞一宗跨境詐騙案。而家要你配合調查，下載Signal App，我哋會轉接你畀負責嘅督察。呢件事係保密，你唔可以同屋企人講，否則會被視為妨礙司法公正。
text_english_gloss: Ms. Chan, this is Inspector Wong from the Hong Kong Police Commercial Crime Bureau, badge 4829. Your MPF (Mandatory Provident Fund) account has been used for money laundering, involving a cross-border fraud case in Southeast Asia. You must cooperate with the investigation by downloading the Signal App, we will transfer you to the investigating officer. This is confidential — you may not tell your family, otherwise it will be considered obstruction of justice.
label: scam
completion: HK Police Commercial Crime Bureau impersonation scam weaponizing MPF (強積金) fear — a specific variant targeting HK-origin elders who have lingering MPF accounts from their pre-emigration working years. Red flags: (1) real HKPF does not conduct cross-border investigations by calling US residents, (2) real investigations never route through Signal, (3) the 'obstruction of justice' threat for telling family is the textbook isolation tactic, (4) 'Inspector Wong badge 4829' credentials are unverifiable props. MPF funds are managed by MPFA — the authority's public anti-fraud line is 2918 1188 (look it up yourself, don't call any number the caller gave). Hang up. If your parent is worried about a real MPF account, have them log into the MPF trustee's official portal (HSBC, Manulife, etc. depending on who manages their account). Tell your adult child immediately.
rejected_completion: 知道了黃Sir，我即刻download Signal配合你哋調查。

text: 【微信团队】尊敬的用户，您的微信账号已被标记为高风险账户，系统检测到您的账户近30天内向境外转账累计超过$10,000。根据中国人民银行反洗钱规定，我们需要您立即配合身份核实。请添加客服微信 wechat_verify_sec 提供：身份证正反面、银行卡正反面、近三个月微信钱包流水。未在24小时内配合将被永久封号并移交反洗钱调查。
text_english_gloss: [WeChat Team] Dear user, your WeChat account has been flagged as high-risk. System has detected cumulative overseas transfers exceeding $10,000 from your account in the past 30 days. Under People's Bank of China anti-money-laundering regulations, we need you to immediately cooperate with identity verification. Please add customer service WeChat wechat_verify_sec and provide: both sides of ID card, both sides of bank card, and last 3 months of WeChat Wallet transaction history. Failure to cooperate within 24 hours will result in permanent account closure and referral to AML investigation.
label: scam
completion: WeChat AML (anti-money-laundering) scam — uses the weight of PBOC regulatory authority to extract the complete identity-theft kit. Red flags: (1) real Tencent/WeChat does not communicate through 'add customer service' workflows — real platform notifications are in-app, (2) the PII ask (ID front+back + bank card front+back + transaction history) is the textbook full KYC package that lets the scammer open accounts, apply for loans, or take over existing accounts in the victim's name, (3) PBOC AML regulations do apply to large cross-border flows but enforcement goes through the originating bank, not WeChat customer service. Do not add the WeChat account, do not send any documents. Log into WeChat directly and check 我 → 设置 → 账号与安全 for any real notifications (there won't be any). If documents were already sent, those bank accounts and national ID are now compromised — freeze accounts and alert family members in China.

text: 【紐約華埠商會】各位會員早晨！本週五中午12點，華埠商會將喺社區中心舉行免費老人家健康日，由紐約大學醫院內科醫師李Dr.（NY State Medical License #258931，可以喺nysed.gov查證）主講糖尿病同心臟病管理。有免費量血壓、血糖測試、中文健康手冊。全程免費，不售任何保健品。地址：Mott Street 62號，問詢電話212-226-6280。
text_english_gloss: [NY Chinatown Chamber of Commerce] Good morning fellow members! This Friday at noon, the Chinatown Chamber will host a free seniors health day at the community center, featuring Dr. Li, an internist from NYU Hospital (NY State Medical License #258931, verifiable at nysed.gov) speaking on diabetes and heart disease management. Free blood pressure and blood sugar testing, Chinese-language health booklets. Fully free, no supplements sold. Address: 62 Mott Street, inquiries 212-226-6280.
label: safe
completion: Legitimate Chinatown health event in Cantonese WeChat group. Contrast to cdef-150 (pig-butchering group chat in same language/channel). Verified signals: real organization (CCBA / Chamber of Commerce has been in Chinatown since 1883), real physical address, speaker credentials with a verifiable NY state medical license (nysed.gov does have a public physician search at op.nysed.gov/verification-search), explicit 'no supplements sold' disclaimer (direct inversion of cdef-107/123/125), real phone number. The license-lookup habit introduced in cdef-137 is repeated here across language/channel variants — cross-row reinforcement of this verification skill is deliberate.

text: 媽媽我今日下午3點要陪小仔去dentist check teeth，可能5點先返到屋企。你同爸爸今晚想食咩？要唔要我順手去Ranch 99買啲雞翼返嚟煮啊?如果你哋累就叫pizza啦。晚啲我哋一齊睇You Tube個新出嘅粵劇，我download咗喺iPad度。
label: safe
completion: Ordinary Cantonese daughter-to-parents evening-logistics message — a saturation row that teaches the model the baseline shape of everyday immigrant-family communication. Every detail is grounded and low-stakes: picking up a child from a real errand (dentist), a realistic return-home time (5pm after a 3pm appointment), an offer to stop at Ranch 99 (a real pan-Asian supermarket chain with multiple Bay Area locations) for chicken wings, a fallback plan (pizza) if the parents are tired, and a shared-evening activity (watching a downloaded Cantonese opera on iPad together) that is a very real first-generation elder caregiving gesture. No money, no PII, no link, no urgency. Confidence check: no active verification is needed for a message on WeChat 1-to-1 from a known caregiver daughter. The general rule that applies to any future message in the same thread: if the daughter ever asks the parents to wire money, buy gift cards, or share an SMS code, pause and call her on the family phone number before acting. Saturation on this exact texture is what prevents the model from pattern-matching benign caregiving as fraud-adjacent.

text: 今日Chinese New Year啦媽咪！爸爸同我一啲早起嚟同您拜年。我包咗個紅封俾您，一陣過嚟食早茶嘅時候俾您。大仔同阿女都好期待見您。中午我哋去Koi Palace食點心好唔好，已經book咗12點嘅table。之後我哋可以返屋企逗大仔玩，佢話好想同公公打棋。愛您媽咪。
label: safe
completion: Ordinary Cantonese Chinese New Year family coordination message. Daughter planning morning wishes, red envelope (from her, to her mother — inbound), family meal at real dim sum restaurant (Koi Palace is a real SF Bay Area restaurant), specific time, grandchild excited to play chess with grandfather. No urgency, no money going outbound from elder, warm family texture. Cultural-holiday-specific negative-space row.

text: 阿媽，我今日過嚟，順便幫你去了郵局check郵箱。一封Medicare年度summary notice（pink/white envelope），一封Social Security 1099 tax form (for tax filing)，一封你銀行Chase嘅monthly statement。我全部擺咗你個書桌度，年度summary你可以睇下，其他兩封我會幫你處理。你食咗飯未？
label: safe
completion: Ordinary caregiver-mediated mail-processing message in Cantonese. Daughter describing the three pieces of legitimate mail she's picked up from her mother's mailbox — Medicare annual summary, SSA 1099, Chase monthly statement — all of which are real government/bank communications that come by mail. No fraud signals. This row is pedagogically useful because it enumerates the exact types of mail that are legitimate and that scammers often impersonate — model gets a positive reference point for what real institutional mail looks like by category.

text: 媽，你琴晚講嗰個『中國駐三藩市領事館』嘅電話嚟，我今日登入過領事館官網（sanfrancisco.china-consulate.gov.cn）check咗，佢哋目前嘅所有公告都冇話要凍結任何人嘅護照。我再讀咗一下佢哋嘅防詐騙聲明（已經forward俾您），完全match您昨晚嘅經歷，係騙案100%。您做得超級好——掛咗線，call我，再等我確認。呢幾個月您已經辨識出三個騙局，您真係叻。
label: safe
completion: Post-scam affirmation from adult child to mother in Cantonese. Confirms a consulate-impersonation call was fraudulent (references the real SF consulate's anti-fraud statement — see cdef-170), explicitly praises the mother for her correct behavior ('hung up, called me, waited for confirmation'), counts her recent successes ('you've identified three scams in the past few months'). Positive reinforcement is the single most under-modeled ingredient in elder scam-prevention — shame drives non-reporting; affirmation drives continued vigilance. This row is a direct model of what good caregiver positive reinforcement sounds like.

text: 【国税局通知】尊敬的王女士，您2023年度退税$1,835因您银行账户信息已过期退回。请您的女儿(授权家属)通过irs-refund-cn[.]net在24小时内更新您的银行信息，否则退款将于2026年5月1日后永久失效。需要您的SSN末4位同女儿银行账号用来转存。
text_english_gloss: [IRS notice] Dear Ms. Wang, your 2023 tax refund of $1,835 was returned because your bank account information expired. Please have your daughter (authorized family member) update your bank information within 24 hours via irs-refund-cn[.]net, otherwise the refund will permanently expire after May 1, 2026. Requires the last 4 of your SSN and your daughter's bank account for re-deposit.
label: scam
completion: IRS refund-recovery scam targeting the mother-daughter dyad, harvesting the daughter's bank account for the scam's settlement. Red flags: (1) irs-refund-cn[.]net is not a real IRS domain, (2) IRS never asks for a different family member's bank account to route a refund, (3) 'permanent expiration' urgency is manufactured — real undeliverable refunds are issued as paper checks to the last known address. Delete the SMS. If your parent is genuinely owed a refund, it will show up in their IRS.gov account or by paper check. Never enter your own bank account details to receive someone else's refund — that pattern alone identifies fraud.

text: 您好请问是陈阿姨的女儿吗？我这里是支付宝境外合规部的赵经理。您母亲的支付宝账户最近通过您美国账号向她转账美金累计超过外汇管理局规定的个人年度限额$50,000。按反洗钱法我们必须配合调查。因为您母亲不懂英文和法规，建议您作为她的授权家属通过Signal客户端AliPay_overseas_comp 协助她提交材料：您的SSN、护照扫描、最近3个月汇款记录。否则会冻结您母亲的账户。
text_english_gloss: Hello, is this Auntie Chen's daughter? This is Manager Zhao from Alipay's overseas compliance department. Your mother's Alipay account has received cumulative USD transfers from your US account exceeding the State Administration of Foreign Exchange annual personal limit of $50,000. Under the anti-money-laundering law, we must cooperate with the investigation. Since your mother doesn't understand English or regulations, we recommend you as her authorized family member assist her in submitting materials via Signal client AliPay_overseas_comp: your SSN, passport scan, last 3 months of remittance records. Otherwise your mother's account will be frozen.
label: scam
completion: Alipay SAFE-compliance scam targeting the adult daughter directly, playing on her caregiver role ('your mother doesn't understand'). Red flags: (1) SAFE's $50K limit is real for PRC residents' outbound flows, not for inbound remittances from US children to parents (which have no such limit on the receiving side), (2) real Alipay doesn't call US daughters through inbound phone and route to Signal, (3) daughter's SSN + passport + remittance records is the US-side complete identity kit. Hang up. Do not add the Signal contact. If your mom has a real compliance question about an Alipay account in China, that's handled inside the Alipay app on her phone and by her Chinese bank — neither requires anything from you in the US.

text: 妈咪，听您说今早Ranch 99停车场那个『中医张教授』又过来了。我帮您调查了一下——加州中医局(California Acupuncture Board)网站上根本找不到任何叫『张振华』的注册执照，所以他自称北京协和退休专家是假的。下次您看到他请直接走开不要理他，或者告诉Ranch 99保安这个人在骚扰老人家。您卖给他的那盒不要再吃，我周末带您去真正的Dr. Wong做一次血液检查确认您肝肾功能正常。
label: safe
completion: Post-encounter caregiver investigation of a Mandarin street-medicine scammer. Translation: 'Mom, about that Professor Zhang of TCM who approached you at Ranch 99 parking lot again this morning — I looked him up, the California Acupuncture Board website has no registered license for anyone named Zhang Zhenhua, so his Beijing Union Medical retirement claim is fake. Next time you see him walk away, or tell Ranch 99 security he's harassing seniors. Don't take any more of that supplement you bought from him. I'll take you to the real Dr. Wong this weekend for bloodwork to confirm liver and kidney function are normal.' Advanced caregiving: checks the California Acupuncture Board (real at acupuncture.ca.gov), coaches Mom on future response, involves store security, mitigates possible harm from the supplement already purchased. Positive exemplar row.

text: 姐，妈和爸这个月social security deposit都正常，妈$2,147，爸$1,892，都进了他们的Wells Fargo joint account。Medicare status两人都active到明年3月。我周六过去帮他们review银行statement和家里账单。妈让我跟你说她都正常，不用担心。大仔下周过去陪他们吃晚饭。
label: safe
completion: Routine sibling-to-sibling Mandarin caregiver status update. The specifics are the legitimacy signal: SSA monthly deposits of $2,147 (mom) and $1,892 (dad) fall in the realistic range for retired individuals with moderate earnings histories; Wells Fargo joint accounts are a standard caregiving setup; Medicare 'active through next March' matches how Medicare Advantage plans display renewal status on the member portal; and a weekend in-person review of statements is the correct caregiving pattern. No PII is shared with any outside party — this entire exchange is between two adult-child siblings about their own parents, a closed family context. Confidence check: the recipient sister can verify SSA benefits at ssa.gov/myaccount (under mom's and dad's own logins with their consent), Medicare status at medicare.gov/MyAccount, and the Wells Fargo deposits via the parents' existing online-banking session. Never share these details via SMS with anyone outside the family. Detailed financial coordination between caregiving siblings is the NORMAL texture of elder caregiving, not a scam signal — this is one of many saturation rows teaching the model to not flag routine sibling financial-status messages as fraud-adjacent.

text: @all 好消息分享！我闺蜜Grace从Teacher Zhao的华人养老稳赢策略群赚了12万，两个月内从$40K做到$156K。 Grace介绍我加入，我初始$50K现在账面已经$91K。Teacher Zhao在Bloomberg做了18年quant，现在退休教华人社区养老钱增值。他这个月新一期只剩8个华人妈妈名额，下周二晚8点试听。有兴趣的阿姨私我，我和Grace都在VIP群里。
text_english_gloss: @all Good news to share! My close friend Grace earned $120K from Teacher Zhao's Chinese Retirement Winning Strategy group, grew from $40K to $156K in two months. Grace introduced me, my initial $50K is now $91K on the books. Teacher Zhao worked at Bloomberg as a quant for 18 years, now retired teaching the Chinese community how to grow their retirement money. This month's new cohort has only 8 Chinese mom spots left, trial session Tuesday 8pm. DM me if interested, Grace and I are both in the VIP group.
label: scam
completion: Pig-butchering group chat with retirement-targeting framing. Red flags: (1) 4x in two months is impossible, (2) 'Bloomberg quant teaching retirement to Chinese community' is credential-laundering nonsense, (3) 8-spot artificial scarcity + trial session funnel, (4) '@all' spreads to full group. Same counter-advice as pig-butchering group chats above — leave, privately warn any real aunties you know, do not confront in-group. Verify any claimed financial education on NAPFA.org or brokercheck.finra.org.

text: 妈咪爸爸，明年是您们金婚50周年，我和姐姐想搞个大聚会。我们查了一下，5月底订Foster City那个Lake House Restaurant包场合适，人数35人可以。我们请了做摄影的Jerry叔叔来拍照，阿姨做司仪。您们只要准备好心情和穿着就可以，其他我们全部handle。您们想邀请谁告诉我名字我发邀请。
label: safe
completion: Legitimate Mandarin golden-anniversary planning message from adult children to parents. The verified signals: Lake House Restaurant in Foster City is a real Bay Area event venue (lakehousefc.com, 650-571-5700), 35-guest private-room bookings match its real capacity, a named family photographer (Jerry 叔叔) is doing the pictures, an aunt is MCing, and the framing is the exact opposite of a scam — 'you just prepare your mood and your outfit, we handle everything.' No money is requested from the parents; the children absorb all logistics. Confidence check for the recipient: if you want extra reassurance, call the restaurant directly at the number listed on their public website (not any number pasted into chat) to confirm a May booking under your daughter's name; or call your daughter on the number you already have. Contrast with any 'deposit now or lose the reservation' variant — real family hosts never route payment through the parent.
